thinking_text:
**Evaluating boundary matching**

I'm considering whether I can safely infer the full boundary. The idea of "matching outer shape to outer contour" makes sense since it implies that the footprint boundary aligns. Yet, I'm wondering about the exact 3D curvature and surface details. It mentions that the outer surface should sit flush, which leads me to think the contact surface conforms. However, does "matching outer shape" mean I only need to look at the perimeter, or should I consider the full surface? It's a bit ambiguous semantically and geometrically.
**Clarifying ontology classes**

I'm thinking about ontology classes and how they focus on target outcomes and functions. That's a good thing! It’s important to have a precise structure in JSON without any extra fields. I want to make sure everything is neat and organized, as it helps in understanding the data better. Keeping things straightforward is the key, especially when handling information like this! I'm feeling good about this clarity on structure!

request.raw_text: Create two cover parts, that have matching outer shape to the outer contour of the central part, sit flush on its outer surface and its counterpart on the other side and have thickness of 0,254cm
reference_geometry_words: outer contour of the central part

aim.primary_aim: Add two cover parts that match the central part's outer contour, sit flush on opposite outer sides, and each have a thickness of 0.254 cm.

functional_design_intentions.name: Opposed covering
functional_design_intentions.description: Provide matching covers for two opposite outer sides of the central part.

functional_design_intentions.name: Flush fit
functional_design_intentions.description: Ensure each cover fits flush against its corresponding outer surface of the central part.

targets_to_change.reference_geometry: Two new cover parts corresponding to opposite outer sides of the central part

required_relationships.reference: outer contour of the central part
corresponding outer surface of the central part
the other side of the central part

targets_to_preserve.reference_geometry: Central part and all other non-targeted geometry
targets_to_preserve.preservation_rule: Preserve the central part, including its referenced outer contour and outer surfaces, and leave all other non-targeted geometry unchanged.

geometry.description: The final model contains two cover parts, each matching the outer contour of the central part, with one flush against a corresponding outer surface and the counterpart flush on the other side.

relationships.reference: outer contour of the central part
corresponding outer surface of the central part

functions.name: Cover opposite sides
functions.description: The two parts provide matching covers on opposite outer sides of the central part.

validation_criteria.description: Exactly two cover parts exist in the final model.
Each cover part has the requested thickness.
The outer shape of each cover matches the outer contour of the central part.
Each cover sits flush against its corresponding outer surface of the central part, with the counterpart located on the other side.
The two new parts serve as covers for opposite sides of the central part.
The central part, its referenced contour and surfaces, and all other non-targeted geometry remain unchanged.

unresolved_requirements.description: The request identifies the existing reference only as the central part and supplies no exact section or feature IDs.
candidate_interpretations: The centrally positioned part in the model
A part already designated as the central part by model semantics or naming

unresolved_requirements.description: The exact pair of outer surfaces intended by 'its outer surface' and 'the other side' is not explicitly identified.
candidate_interpretations: Two geometrically opposite outer surfaces of the central part
The two principal side surfaces intended to receive covers

unresolved_requirements.description: It is unclear whether matching the outer shape requires only matching the boundary contour or also conforming to any nonplanar surface shape.
candidate_interpretations: Each cover has a perimeter matching the central part's outer contour
Each cover fully conforms to the corresponding outer surface while retaining the matching perimeter
